summary: The root دَبَب primarily refers to slow, soft, or gentle movement, like a child crawling or an old person walking. It can also describe the movement of insects or small creatures.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.

headwords.def: دَبَّ دب aor. دَبِبَ , inf. n. دَبِيبٌ (T, S, M, Msb, K, &c.) and دَبٌّ (M, K,) and مَدَبٌّ , (S, K,) [and perhaps دَبَبٌ also, q. v.,] It, or he, (the ant, T, M, and any animal, M, and in like manner a party moving towards the enemy, T, or an army, and a child, Msb,) [ crept; crawled; or] went, or walked, leisurely, or gently, (T, M, Msb, K,) without haste, (T,) عَلَى الأَرْضِ [ upon the ground ]: (S:) and [simply] he walked: (IAar, T:) he (an old man) [ crept along; or] walked leisurely, softly, or gently: (S:) and , also, he walked leisurely, by slow degrees. (TA.) Hence, أَكْذَبُ مَنْ دَبَّ وَدَرَجَ The most lying of those who have walked and died, or passed away, or perished: (T:) i. e., of the living and the dead. (T, S, K.) And يَدِبُّ مَعَ القُرَادِ
دَبَّبَ see 1, first sentence.

headwords.def: دَبَّةٌ دب دبه دبة A single act [ of creeping, or crawling, or] of going, or walking, leisurely, or gently: pl. دِبَابٌ . (K.) A hill, or heap, or gibbous hill, syn. كَثِيب , (IAar, T, S, M, K,) of sand: (S, K:) and (in some copies of the K “ or ”) a tract of red sand: or an even tract of sand: (K:) or, as in some copies of the K, an even tract of land: (TA:) and a place abounding in sand: (T, L:) pl. as above. Such a one fell into, or upon, a place abounding in sand ]; meaning, (tropical:) into difficulty, or misfortune; for the camel in such a place suffers fatigue. (T.)
